# iaas_microvm_snapshot (Resource)

Saves the disk of a sandbox as a snapshot and keeps it until destroyed. Memory is not saved: a sandbox started from the snapshot (iaas_microvm snapshot_id) boots cold from the saved disk. The platform takes the snapshot asynchronously; create waits until it is ready and fails with the platform's reason if it fails. A snapshot is stored in the location it was taken in, billed per GiB-hour of the space it uses until it is destroyed, and survives the deletion of its sandbox. A snapshot cannot be changed: every argument forces a new snapshot. Import by id; import reads sandbox_id from the platform (null when the sandbox is deleted) and leaves description and consistency null until configured, which adopts the configured value without replacing the snapshot.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Save the disk of a sandbox. Create waits until the snapshot is ready. On locations without a fast-copy file
# system a running sandbox may pause for a few seconds (see paused_ms); pause or stop it first to avoid that.
resource "iaas_microvm_snapshot" "golden" {
  sandbox_id  = iaas_microvm.base.id
  name        = "golden-image"
  description = "Installed and configured, before the first customer job"
}

output "snapshot_disk_gib" {
  value = iaas_microvm_snapshot.golden.disk_gib
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique per account: 1-64 characters of lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. Changing it forces a new snapshot.
- `sandbox_id` (String) UUID of the sandbox to snapshot (running, paused or stopped). Changing it forces a new snapshot.

### Optional

- `consistency` (String) Requested consistency: auto (default), quiesced (fails when the file systems cannot be quiesced) or crash. The platform reports what it achieved in consistency_achieved.
- `description` (String) Free text, up to 255 characters. The platform does not return it on import; configure it to adopt it.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `billable_gib` (Number) Whole GiB billed per hour.
- `capture_method` (String) reflink, paused_copy or offline_copy; empty when the location does not report it.
- `consistency_achieved` (String) quiesced, crash or clean.
- `created_at` (String) When the snapshot was requested.
- `disk_gib` (Number) Disk size in GiB; a sandbox started from the snapshot needs a plan with at least this much disk.
- `id` (String) Snapshot UUID.
- `image_id` (String) Image the source sandbox ran.
- `kind` (String) Snapshot kind: disk.
- `location_id` (String) Location the snapshot is stored in; a sandbox started from it runs there.
- `mem_mib` (Number) Memory of the source sandbox in MiB.
- `paused_ms` (Number) Milliseconds the sandbox was paused for the snapshot; null when the location does not report it.
- `price_gib_hour` (Number) Price per GiB-hour of stored snapshot space in the snapshot's location (0 = free).
- `ready_at` (String) When the snapshot became ready (billing starts).
- `size_bytes` (Number) Disk size of the snapshot in bytes.
- `source_state` (String) State of the sandbox when it was snapshotted: running, paused or stopped.
- `status` (String) creating, ready, failed, deleting or unavailable. A failed or deleting snapshot is dropped from state on refresh.
- `used_bytes` (Number) Bytes the snapshot actually stores (what is billed, rounded up to whole GiB).
- `vcpu` (Number) vCPUs of the source sandbox.
- `volumes_excluded` (Number) How many data volumes the sandbox had attached that are NOT in this snapshot (a snapshot holds the root disk only); 0 when none.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by snapshot UUID. sandbox_id is read from the platform; description and consistency are not returned,
# so configure them to adopt them (this does not replace the snapshot).
terraform import iaas_microvm_snapshot.golden 5c0d7a52-3e8f-4a8e-9c31-2f6a7b8c9d01
```
